Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testPreserveDOM()` calls `doTest("preserve", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, " foo ")` which tests that the value retrieved from the XML via JXPath includes leading and trailing spaces (" foo "). The current bug report states that JXPath automatically trims string values and thus the leading and trailing spaces are stripped off, returning "foo" instead of " foo ". The test uses a `DocumentContainer` initialized with a model "DOM" and XML resource "XmlSpace.xml". The `doTest` method creates a `JXPathContext` with a document container and verifies the value at a specified XPath. The bug lies in how the XML document is parsed and values extracted: somewhere in the pipeline (likely in the XML parsing or value extraction step), string values are trimmed. The parsing method `parseXML` in `DocumentContainer` configures the XML parser but does not indicate trimming here. However, the document model "DOM" could be causing whitespace normalization or trimming. The root cause is likely that the "DOM" model or the XML parser used by JXPath implicitly trims or normalizes text nodes, thus leading to the removal of leading and trailing whitespace when string values are retrieved. This behavior contradicts expectations for preserving exact string values from XML.

Because no recent similar bug reports are found, this diagnosis relies on understanding the test, the bug report, and the XML parsing behavior used.

Next step would be to check if the XML parser or the DOM model used in `DocumentContainer` enforces whitespace normalization or trimming that causes JXPath to lose the leading/trailing spaces. Fixing it would involve altering XML parsing or string value extraction to preserve whitespace exactly as required.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
